unit.why: A short anecdote: the Besht welcomes the Sabbath in a field, the sheep there stand up on their hind legs, and the text adds an explanation of why.
unit.boundary_note: The heading 'מענין קדושת כתר' at the end belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי אומרים בשם הבעש״ט הק׳ זי״ע
stories.summary_en: When the Besht welcomed the Sabbath in a field, the flock of sheep stood up on their hind legs like men, which is explained as his raising the whole world to its source.

tags.why: The scene is the welcoming of the Sabbath (kabbalat Shabbat).

quotes: ועמדו רק על שני רגלים האחרונים כעמידת איש
tags.why: The animals stand upright like men, a wonder.
He recites the kabbalat Shabbat prayers.

quotes: והעלה בשעת מעשה את כל העולם למקורו הראשון
tags.why: His holy worship raises the world to its source.

quotes: ואומרים בשם צדיקים טעמו ונימוקו עמו
tags.why: The anecdote is wrapped in a long explanation of its meaning.
The story shows how great the Besht's holiness was.

quotes: ששמע ואת מפי הה״ק מרוזין זצ״ל
tags.why: The story is framed as told by the Rizhiner.

missing_concepts: animals responding to a tsaddik's holiness
raising of creation / the life-force in things to its source
